Highlights:
# Rocket 4 Plus - G Support documentation? 

- S

 Steve 

 12/16/22, 5:27 PM 

Would anyone be able to provide the appropriate documentation for the new Rocket 4 Plus - G or a link for me to obtain it? I just received mine and I want to make sure that any judgement I make plays fair. Also, in case it isn't there, since the 2TB and 4TB models are dual-sided, do you folks recommend proper thermal contact via thermal pads between the drive and the m.2 slot's pcb? If so, can you provide a recommended pad thickness?

...

---
- S

 Sabrent Admin Staff

 12/18/22, 7:45 PM 

@Steve If you mean the specs and you received the 4TB model, it should be similar to the updated Rocket 4 Plus:

Up to 7200/6850 MB/s, 940K/1000K 4K IOPS, 3000TBW

I will also pass on the suggestion that we do a datasheet, although usually we do provide a table with explicit specifications. I will ask about the cooling but it is best to at least cool the controller, if possible, and the M.2 spec for SSDs has a defined maximum height for dual-sided drives that should assist you in determining thermal pad thickness for the rear.

...

Sabrent Admin Staff

 12/18/22, 8:38 PM 

@Steve Reading up on this it seems the specifications for M.2 vary. Typically the PCB is 0.8mm +/- 10%, the M.2 socket is 2.25mm center, and the rear componentry is 1.35mm. Thermal padding of 0.5mm should work but 0.75mm may be better for maximum pressure. This is something I will try to have our team test.

---

SABRENT ROCKET 4 PLUS-G SERIES INSTALLATION GUIDE

IMPORTANT INFORMATION, PLEASE NOTICE

When installing any PCle Gen 4 NVMe SSD directly onto a PCle GEN 4 motherboard, A HEATSINK IS REQUIRED TO DISSIPATE THE HEAT GENERATED BY THE DRIVE'S EXTREME SPEED LEVELS TO AVOID THERMAL THROTTLING AND TO MAXIMIZE THE PERFORMANCE. Many PCle GEN 4 motherboards are sold with a built-in heatsink, so you're good to go without an aftermarket heatsink. Just follow the manufacturer's user manual for the installation instructions. If your motherboard does not have a built-in heatsink, we recommend using the Sabrent Rocket Heatsink for optimal performance.

PCle Gend NVMe SSDs generate excessive heat. To help dissipate the heat, Sabrent has developed a state-of-the-art heatsink using the winning combination of copper and aluminum. The copper is used to absorb the neal from the drive, spreading it up to the grooved aluminum, giving the heat more air surface to cool off, therefore avoiding thermal throttling and maximizing the performance of your drive.

SABRENT ROCKET 4 PLUS-6 M.2 NVMe SSD Installation Guide as a Secondary Drive

1. Attach the Sabrent ROCKET 4 PLUS-G M.2 NVMe SSD as a secondary drive and load Windows® from your existing drive.

2.In Windows 8® and later, move the mouse to the lower left corner of your desktop and right click on the Start lcon, then select ‘Disk Management'.

3. When Disk Management opens, a pop-up should appear and prompt you to initialize the SSD.

4. Select MBR (Master Boot Record) or GUID partition table (GPT) and click OK. MBR is best for certain legacy software compatibility, while GPT is better for modern systems.

5. Right click in the area that says Unallocated and select New Simple Volume...

6. The New Simple Volume Wizard will open, click Next

7. Leave the Specify Volume Size as the maximum (default value) and click Next

8. Select a Drive Letter and click Next

9. In the Format Partition screen, decide on a Volume label (the name you want to give the drive) and click Next The drive is now formatted and ready for use
